newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RALLYING-SAINZ IN CHARGE WITH MCRAE AND MAKINEN OUT.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-SAINZ IN CHARGE WITH MCRAE AND MAKINEN OUT.

text.p: Spaniard Carlos Sainz took charge of the New Zealand rally on Sunday after Briton Colin McRae and defending world champion and current series leader Tommi Makinen of Finland had been forced to retire during a dramatic first leg.

Sainz, in his Ford Escort car, was delighted with the course of events which boosted his hopes of a third world title after he demonstrated his mastery of the muddy tracks through the forests near Maungaturoto, north of Auckland.

"It was a very tough day," he said. "It was very competitive, but for us the end result is very pleasing. The wet and muddy conditions were demanding and difficult and we had to drive very hard, with great concentration, to finish the day in this position.
"Tomorrow (Monday) is the longest day of the event, but I think the narrower and twistier stages to the south of Auckland will suit us better because the Escort's chassis is so good.

"The new modifications made to the car recently, especially the six speed gearbox, worked really well and I felt we had very little to worry about with the car today, except to keep washing the mud off!"
Sainz, a three-times winner of the rally, had spent much of the opening day in the chase behind the pace-setting duel of McRae, in his Subaru, and Makkinen, in his Mitsubishi.

As expected, they dominated the early proceedings and broke a succession of records. McRae, seeking his fourth win in five years in New Zealand, led from the start but came unstuck after establishing a 57-second lead in the eighth of the 10 stages in the first leg. The full rally consists of 24.

By then, however, Makinen had already been removed from the fray after rolling out of the contest on only the fourth stage of the day. His departure left McRae with a comfortable-looking position, a good lead and a straightforward opportunity to revive his title challenge.

"We were 14 kilometres into the section when the car mysteriously slowed down and came to a halt," said McRae. "It was very frustrating. After having a good look, we found it was a failure of a cam belt pulley on the engine and that was it.

"With such a big lead, I felt we were on course for a much needed win and 10 valuable points, but it was not to be. Fortunately for us, however, Tommi has not scored any points either so it is not as bad as it could be."

A Sainz victory would lift him to second place between the two in the championship standings and give the Spaniard a great opportunity to press home his challenge. Makinen currently leads with 42 while McRae has 32 and Sainz 28 points.
"There is still a long way to go," warned Sainz and co-driver Luis Moya. "There are two more tough days before the end of this rally and anything can happen."
